Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.077 of 2023 at Police Station-Obra, District-Sonbhadra under Sections 304B, 498A, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 06.04.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 08.08.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Ajay Srivastava, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA from the record,
entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant never harassed the deceased nor demanded dowry.
3. The applicant resided at Mumbai where he worked for a living.
The deceased wanted to live in city with him and the applicant could not accede to her wishes because of financial constraints.
The deceased became depressed by the prolonged separation from her husband.
4. On the fateful day, the deceased succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
5. The post mortem report opines that the cause of death is asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

6. Injuries depicted in the post mortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i). Nature of ligature mark.
(ii).
The hyoid bone was intact.
7. The applicant did not abet or instigate the deceased to commit suicide.
8. The prerequisites for attracting the presumptions under Section 304B IPC are not made out in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
In light of the above stated arguments and considering the fact that the applicant has been in jail for 8 years, the criminal history will not come in the way of grant of bail.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Anil Prasad be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
